newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore power demand seen growing 7.3 pct yearly.
newsitem.headline: Singapore power demand seen growing 7.3 pct yearly.

text.p: Demand for power generation in Singapore is likely to grow by 7.3 percent until the year 2000, Member of Parliament Yu-Foo Yee Shoon said on Wednesday.

An estimated US$600 billion will be spent on infrastructure in Asia, excluding Japan, over the next few years, with power investments expected to total US$140 billion, she said at the opening of Kohler Power Systems' regional headquarters.

"With a host of power-related companies using Singapore as a manufacturing and equipment-servicing base ... Kohler will be able to tap on the resources and capabilities of this industry to fuel its growth," Yu-Foo said.
Power generation in Singapore was a S$10 billion heavy industry, employing more than 40,000 people, Yu-Foo said.
Kohler Power Systems, a unit of Kohler Co. of the United States, manufactures engines, generators and electrical components.
It opened a US$10 million manufacturing plant here and targets US$50 million in revenue over the next three years.
